title: Gentiles by Nature We Belong
description: Gentiles by Nature We Belong in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 114, headed “The same, Rom. 11. 16 17”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Gen-tiles by na-ture we be-long To the wild o-live wood; Grace took us from the bar-ren tree, And grafts us in the good.

lines: Grace took us from the barren tree,
And grafts us in the good.
With the same blessings grace endows
If pure and holy be the root,
Then let the children of the saints
Pour out thy Spirit on them, Lord,
And wash them in thy blood.
Thus to the parents and their seed
And numerous households meet at last

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
